caption.text:
Thank you to everyone who has shared kind words, stories, and memories of Joe. Please keep them coming—they are helping more than you know.

What is not helping, and what Joe would have been absolutely ashamed and disgusted by, are the false narratives, assumptions, and speculation that are already circulating.

I understand Joe meant a great deal to many of you, and that’s exactly why I chose to share this news. But there is a real family trying to process an unimaginable loss, and social media rumors that flow into local real life should be the last thing we have to deal with right now.

I promise that, when the time is right, the truth will come. Right now is not that time.

Until then, honor the man instead of feeding the rumor mill. Respect the family he loved and the people he leaves behind. Think before you speak. If you weren’t shoulder to shoulder with him- you likely don’t know the whole story—and it’s not your place to fill in the blanks.

Respectfully
-Alx

#joefelz

With word rapidly spreading, I wanted to put out a formal statement.

Joe Felz has left this earth and has finally found his free. 

I don’t have many words right now, but I ask that you please give myself, Joe’s family, and all of his loved ones the space and time needed to process a loss of this magnitude.

I also want to pass along a message from Brandy that I hope everyone will keep in mind:

“The manner in which something occurs should never overshadow the end result or the legacy that is left behind. Think before you speak. Consider who will hear your words, and honor those who have yet to speak.”

Thank you for your prayers, your love, your understanding, and for remembering Joe for the life he lived #joefelz

caption.text:
🇨🇷Reality Check… Who’s ready to live Pura Vida?🌴

As you guys know- Joe is currently on an extended media break. The reality is… the matrix has unfortunately sunk its nails back in, and it looks like we’ll be stationary in the U.S. for at least the next year. We’ve got a lot here that simply has to be handled

Our homestead in Costa Rica hasn’t just been a breath of fresh mountain air for us—it has become a beacon of hope for so many of you. It’s been proof that a different way of living is possible. That you don’t have to be wealthy, retired, or special to build a life that’s slower, simpler, and more intentional. That there really is another way to live.

I simply cannot sit with the thought of a place with that much life, energy, peace, and love to give… just sitting there. Breaks my heart. So I’m putting out the feelers. I’m brainstorming.

What if, while we’re tied up here in the U.S., there were people who truly resonated with this way of life and wanted to continue living the vision at Reality? Maybe one family. Maybe two. Maybe even three. Not tourists. Not people looking for an inexpensive tropical escape.

People who genuinely want to live simple live free contribute, build, care for the land, and be part of the mission Joe and I started. 

I honestly don’t know exactly what this looks like yet. I’m not announcing a program or making promises. I’m simply looking for conversations with people who feel aligned with the mission and believe in what we’re trying to build.

Reality was never about us. It was always about proving that another way of living is possible

If you have an idea we- lemme hear it

If any of that resonates with you, let’s talk🛖🇨🇷🐓 #homestead #offgrid #costarica #puravida #joeandalx

caption.text:
Father’s Day, for me, isn’t just about fathers.

It’s about the mothers who stepped into both roles when a father wasn’t there. The ones who carried the weight of two parents, often without recognition, because their children needed them to.

It’s about the sisters who stood beside their sisters in the delivery room when no one else did. The sisters, aunts, grandparents, and family members who showed up for birthdays, holidays, school events, and the everyday moments that matter when someone else chose not to.

It’s about the men who became role models for children who needed one, even when they had no obligation to do so. The coaches, uncles, mentors, family friends, and neighbors who quietly helped shape a life simply by being present.

It’s about the fathers who show up every single day—through the sleepless nights, the sacrifices, the worries, and the responsibilities. The fathers who have had to carry both parental roles when a mother was absent.

It’s also about the fathers who can’t always be physically present because they’re out working long hours, making sacrifices, and doing everything they can to provide a better life for their children.

And it’s about the young men who were forced to grow up too soon, stepping into adult responsibilities and fatherly roles long before they should have had to.

The truth is, raising children has never been a one-person job. It takes love. It takes sacrifice. It takes people showing up for each other.

It takes a whole motherfuckin’ village these days, y’all.

Happy Father’s Day to everyone who stepped up when it mattered. ❤️ #fathers #family #community #thekidswillbealright #joeandalx
